name: Call Ratio Backspread 1x3
summary: Sell one nearer call and buy three further-OTM calls in the same expiry; a more extreme, cheaper-per-long backspread with a deeper valley and steeper upside. Obscure and generally worse risk-adjusted than the 1x2.

legs.strike_rule: Short call ATM, 0.50 delta. Covered by one of the three long calls.
Three long calls at 0.15-0.25 delta, placed far enough out that the package opens near zero cost.

max_profit: unlimited above the long strike, rising at 2x the slope of a 1x2 backspread (net long two calls)
max_loss: (long strike - short strike) * 100 - net credit (or + debit), at the long strike at expiry. Defined.
breakevens: lower: short strike + credit per share; upper: long strike + max loss per share, reached faster than a 1x2 because you own three calls

greeks.gamma: strongly positive above the long strike
greeks.theta: strongly negative -- you are net long two options

typical_dte: 60-120 DTE. The deeper valley and heavier theta demand more time than the 1x2.
when_to_use: Rarely. Only when IV rank is under 20, call skew is flat, and you want maximum convexity per dollar for a specific large-move thesis. The 1x2 gives most of the payoff with materially less theta bleed -- prefer it by default.
entry_rules: MARKED AS AGGRESSIVE -- default to the 1x2 unless the 1x3 prices for a credit AND IV rank < 20.
Short call delta ~0.50; long calls delta 0.15-0.25.
Ratio exactly 1:3. GCD(1,3) = 1, so Alpaca accepts the ratio, and the single short call is covered by one of the three longs -- Level 3 submittable as a single MLeg order.
Package must open for a net credit or a debit <= 5% of (long strike - short strike).
Max loss (width*100 - credit) <= 1.5% of equity (tighter than the 1x2 because the valley is wider and more likely to be reached).
OI >= 1000 on the long strike (you need triple quantity), quoted size >= 30.
management_rules: Take profit at 2.5x the max-loss amount, or on a 2.0 ATR move above the long strike.
Time stop: close at 30 DTE, not 21 -- the extra long option makes late-cycle theta twice as damaging.
Valley stop: at 45 DTE, if the underlying is within 2% of the long strike, close.
If net delta exceeds +1.50 per unit, sell one long call, converting to a 1x2 backspread.
Take the vega profit: if IV rank rises above 50 with price unchanged, close.
exit_rules: Flat by 15:45 ET on expiration day.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: short call ITM at 15:30 ET on expiry day -> close the whole package immediately.
ASSIGNMENT GUARD: short call ITM with extrinsic < $0.10 on any day -> close that session.
DIVIDEND GUARD: close before ex-dividend whenever the short call is ITM and extrinsic < 1.5 * dividend.
Mandatory close at 30 DTE absent a live catalyst.
assignment_risk: Single short call, covered by one of the three longs. Economics bounded; operationally still delivers 100 short shares per unit if assigned. Same guards as the 1x2, applied more strictly because the short strike is fully ATM at entry.
buying_power: Width of the covering vertical: (long strike - short strike)*100 - credit per unit. The two extra long calls add only their premium.
liquidity_needs: Needs a genuinely liquid long strike -- OI >= 1000 and quoted size >= 30, because a 3-lot on an illiquid wing will not fill as a package.
common_mistakes: Using the 1x3 for the extra leverage without accounting for double the theta; opening it inside 60 DTE; letting it decay in the valley; failing to convert to a 1x2 when delta runs.
zero_dte_notes: Not usable. Maximum theta, maximum valley, zero time.
family: Two-leg verticals and same-expiry two-leg combos (call/put verticals, straddles, strangles, guts, synthetics/risk reversals, ratio verticals and backspreads)
